findings.reason: the owner must move to a lower layer both `_schema` and `doccheck` can import (the declarations and `SECTION_DECLARATION_ENUM` already live in `reckon/_schema.py`, the natural home), or the plan ships two cycles.
findings.text: §18 locates the shared "still work" predicate on `reckon/roadmap.py`, whose callers it names as `implementable_sections` (same module), `_schema.plan_executable_remainder` and `doccheck._implementable_section_ids`; but `roadmap.py:21` already does `from reckon._schema import (...)` and `roadmap.py:38` does `from reckon.doccheck import (...)`, so `_schema` importing the predicate from `roadmap` (or `doccheck` doing so) closes an import cycle — the predicate cannot be owned by a module that sits above both of its consumers.

findings.reason: the per-§16/§17/§18 net of "+2" is understated and §18's stated reason for privacy is contradicted by its own caller list; the accounting must be corrected or a same-package owner chosen.
findings.text: §18's interface accounting states "no public definition is added or retired; the predicate is private, because its two callers share the crew package", but the callers it names in the same section are `_schema.plan_executable_remainder` and `doccheck._implementable_section_ids`, neither in `reckon/crew/`; §16's own house rule counts a definition consumed across a package boundary, so §18 adds one to `public_definitions` while claiming it adds none.

findings.reason: the plan must reconcile the two semantics (keep two named predicates, or state the MCP view's rows now filter differently) rather than assert one test.
findings.text: §17 asserts the machinery-region test is "spelled three times" as the span parser's section stack, the prose parser's protected flag, and `mcp_views._inside_structured_region`, all becoming one predicate; the span parser (`reckon/_plan_html.py:60`) and the prose parser (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:209`) test presence of any `data-reckon` attribute, while `mcp_views._inside_structured_region` (`reckon/mcp_views.py:2075`) tests `parent.get("data-reckon") not in (None, "section")` and treats a `data-reckon="section"` element as authored, not machinery — so unifying them as written changes what the MCP view's `_authored_section_headings` walk treats as machinery, a behaviour the plan does not account for.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17's `plan_headings` hides the span parser, the heading-level generalisation, wrapper-id resolution, identity derivation and card recognition behind one named record, a small interface over substantial behaviour.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the shared implementability predicate §18 places on `reckon/roadmap.py` has two of its three named consumers in modules that `roadmap` already imports, so neither can import it back.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — §18 accounts no new public definition, but its own named callers are `reckon/_schema.py` and `reckon/doccheck.py`, outside the crew package, so under §16's stated house rule the predicate crosses a package boundary, earns a public name and is counted; supplied counts public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's prior-art map for the machinery-region test is inaccurate: `mcp_views._inside_structured_region` excludes `data-reckon="section"` while the span and prose parsers protect on mere presence of a `data-reckon` attribute, so §17's "three spellings of one test" is two spellings of one test plus a third that answers a different question.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §18 makes `plan_executable_remainder` express one rule over the existing `implementable_sections` rather than a parallel reader, and states why nothing is retired.
